section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1970
title: ## ALL INDIA SURVEY During 1970, 1,39,752 deaths were reported in India which had resulted from accidents of various types. The causes of accidents have been classified into two broad categories viz. (i) Accidents due to acts of nature such as animal bites/killing, floods, landslides etc. and (ii) Accidents due to other causes such as mishappenings in factories, aircrashes, railway accidents etc. The details are shown in Appendices I and II. The break-up of such accidental deaths in the entire country due to various causes is furnished in Table I. It may be seen that deaths due to acts of nature account for 30.2% and those due to other causes constitute the remaining 69.8% of the total accidental deaths in the country. As observed in previous years also, drowning accounted for a very large number of deaths (27,915) and constituted 20% of the total. Road accidents and accidents on the railways accounted for 7,288 and 8,282 deaths respectively. The pattern of the percentage distribution of accidental deaths due to various causes has been more or less the same as in the past five years, except for accidents on the roads and deaths due to poisoning. The number of deaths due to poisoning has increased from 8,308 during 1969 to 9,738 during 1970. TABLE—I
